newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica eyes 20 year U.S. debt issue later this yr.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica eyes 20 year U.S. debt issue later this yr.

text.p: South Africa's risk profile had improved to such an extent that it hopes to raise a foreign debt issue with a 20 year maturity in the U.S. later this year, finance department director-general Maria Ramos said on Tuesday.
Briefing the parliamentary finance committee on her department's 1997/98 budget, Ramos said this would be part of the planned programme to borrow four billion rand offshore this year.
The government also planned to take a roadshow to Japan in the middle of June to raise money in Japanese Yen in the Samurai market.
"It is a good time to be raising money in yen because their interest rates are really quite low," Ramos said.

"What is particularly satisfying is that as a country we have been able to move from a position where it was difficult to borrow in maturities of five years, to a position where we can easily borrow in maturities of 10 years," she said.
Foreign debt issues already undertaken were also trading well inside their launch prices.

"Our Global, which was launched at 193 basis points, is trading at about 80 basis points. The 10 year issue that we did in the Yankee market last year we launched at 195 and it is now trading at 160 basis points," Ramos said.
South Africa had managed to improve its risk profile and become better known as a participant in the international capital market, she added.
